# ffmpeg.wasm redistribution record

Runtime: unmodified ESM files from `@ffmpeg/ffmpeg@0.12.15` and single-thread `@ffmpeg/core@0.12.10`, downloaded from the official npm registry. No npm installation or lifecycle script was run. `../manifest.json` records tarball SHA-512 integrity and each distributed file's SHA-256. `tools/vendor-ffmpeg.mjs` reproduces these bytes.

- Wrapper license: MIT, reproduced in `wrapper-MIT.txt`.
- Core package license: GPL-2.0-or-later. The GPLv2 text is in `core-COPYING.GPLv2.txt`; FFmpeg's licensing explanation is in `core-LICENSE.md`. The official build enables GPL and external libraries, including x264 and x265. The MIT wrapper does not change the core's license.
- Official combined release: [v12.15](https://github.com/ffmpegwasm/ffmpeg.wasm/releases/tag/v12.15), commit `71aa99d37c02a7b4c435275ca9ef50e612f6efa1`. **Do not substitute v0.12.10**, which contains older package versions.
- Core npm publication timestamp: `2025-01-07T10:13:14.328Z` (official npm registry metadata).
- Same-origin release source: [ffmpeg-wasm-v12.15-source.tar.gz](../sources/ffmpeg-wasm-v12.15-source.tar.gz). It includes the wrapper TypeScript, core bindings, modified FFmpeg command sources, Dockerfile, Makefile and build scripts.
- Same-origin external sources: [source-lock.json](../sources/source-lock.json) lists 18 complete repository archives with exact commits, retrieval URLs, byte counts and SHA-256. These cover FFmpeg, the 15 codec/support libraries in the release recipe, Emscripten (including libc/runtime sources and build tools), and SDL2. Each archive is beside the lock file on this same origin and includes its upstream notices. Test-only submodules omitted by GitHub archives are explicitly listed in the lock. They are not linked into the distributed core.

## Corresponding-source evidence and remaining verification

The npm packages have no `gitHead` metadata. Their exact published tarballs are integrity pinned. The official release identifies the package combination, and the supplied dependency snapshots follow its Dockerfile. All refs were resolved to the latest reachable commit before npm publication. For the mutable x264 `4-cores` and lame `master` refs, current HEAD also equals that pre-publication commit (dated 2022 and 2020 respectively). Emscripten 3.1.40 explicitly pins SDL2 release-2.24.2 with a source hash. This is positive correspondence evidence. The CI recipe nevertheless uses a Docker cache, and the public GitHub Actions API returned no retained runs or build-specific dependency manifest for the release commit during this investigation.

The release archive alone would be incomplete: distribute it together with every source archive, this license record and the source lock. No local modification was made to the runtime. The upstream Makefile (`make prd`), Dockerfile and build scripts specify how to build the single-thread core; use the locked dependency commits when reconstructing their source trees. An independent rebuild was not performed. A byte-identical rebuild is not asserted to be a legal requirement here, and this record does not give a legal compliance determination. Keep the sources available wherever the binary is distributed.

The upstream release recipe references FFmpeg `n5.1.4`, emsdk `3.1.40`, x264 `4-cores`, x265 `3.4`, libvpx `v1.13.1`, lame `master`, Ogg `v1.3.4`, theora `v1.1.1`, opus `v1.3.1`, vorbis `v1.3.3`, zlib `v1.2.11`, libwebp `v1.3.2`, freetype2 `VER-2-10-4`, fribidi `v1.0.9`, harfbuzz `5.2.0`, libass `0.15.0`, and zimg `release-3.0.5` (recursive clone). See the archived Dockerfile for exact repositories and compiler options. SDL2 is obtained by the Emscripten port tool. The source lock and adjacent archives cover these referenced source trees; no external source download is required merely to read them.

Runtime load must explicitly use same-origin coreURL, wasmURL and classWorkerURL. The unchanged wrapper's unused default refers to unpkg core 0.12.9. The application does not use that default; CSP additionally blocks third-party script/worker loading. Media bytes stay in browser worker memory except for the app's separately authorized Google upload operation.
